children: Indx rebuilds a dataset into a fresh versioned table, then atomically swaps the pointer — an in-place reload would wedge the engine.

When the Indx Engine reindexes a Dataset, it never mutates the live index in place. Instead it builds a complete new table named bp_<scope>_vN, fully populates it, and only then flips a persistent_term pointer to the new version atomically. Readers on the old version finish cleanly; the next query lands on vN. An in-place reload would leave the engine serving a half-built index — it wedges — so the indirection through persistent_term is the whole point.

The rebuild runs as a job on the Oban Worker runtime (the :indx queue, IndexerWorker), so it can take its time without blocking HTTP API v1 traffic. It is triggered after content changes flow through the Indx Retriever Seam, and after a Deploy that alters the index shape. The old bp_<scope>_v(N-1) table can be dropped once no reader references it.

The Edge Projector borrows the same rebuild-then-swap discipline when it repopulates the Content Edges Table — derive everything into a new state, swap atomically, never edit live rows under readers. That shared pattern is why both the search index and the Content Graph survive rebuilds without flicker or partial reads.

The <scope> in bp_<scope>_vN is a tenancy key: a rebuild runs for a single Workspace + Project slice, never across tenants, so bp_production_v7 for one tenant and another's are independent shadow tables. Because the swap is atomic and per-scope, LiveView Studio keeps rendering throughout — the Graph View it hosts simply lands on the new version on the next query.
